newsitem.title: ITALY: Albanian parties to sign accord in Rome on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Albanian parties to sign accord in Rome on Monday.

text.p: The leaders of Albania's political parties will meet in Rome on Monday to sign an accord to ensure that forthcoming elections proceed peacefully and fairly, a Roman Catholic peace group said on Saturday.

The Community of Sant'Egidio said that leaders of the main parties, including Tritan Shehu, chairman of the Democratic Party, and Fatos Nano of the Socialists, would gather at its Rome headquarters to sign the agreement.
In the Albanian capital Tirana, Nano confirmed he would be attending the Rome meeting.
"It will be a political and social pact between the parties that the elections will be normal, with guarantees for people not to contest the outcome," Nano told Reuters in an interview.
He said the involvement of the Community of Sant'Egidio, which has a history of brokering international peace deals, would provide additional authority for the agreement.

Officials of President Sali Berisha's right-wing Democratic Party were unavailable for comment. The Democrats are defending a huge parliamentary majority, won in elections last year which were criticised as unfair by the Albanian opposition and international observers.
The Community of Sant'Egidio said the main parties and "the protagonists in the country's current transition" had taken part in drafting the agreement.
The election set for June 29, was called after violence seized the Balkan country in February and March, when hundreds of thousands of people lost money in failed pyramid investment schemes.
Italy is leading a 7,000-strong multinational peacekeeping force to help the impoverished ex-communist nation.
